newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ FUTURES END FIRMER IN LIGHT TRADING.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ FUTURES END FIRMER IN LIGHT TRADING.

text.p: FCOJ futures ended slightly higher in thin dealings on Wednesday, bolstered by local buying, traders said.

September juice settled up 0.45 cent per lb, to 75.60 cents, after ranging from 76.05 to 75.30 cents. November rose 0.65 cent, to 77.75 cents, while the rest of the board closed 0.35 to 0.80 cent firmer.

New York juice futures headed higher at the outset, as locals came in buying, dealers said. Trade selling, however, capped gains and prevented the September contract from making a decisive move above near-term chart resistance at 76.00 cents, they said.
"The locals tried to break 76.00," said one trader. "They got it up to 76.05, but the trade sold it off."
Dealers said much of the day's activity centered on the nearby September/November spread, which was bid at 2.10 and finished at 2.05 compared with 1.95 at the close on Tuesday.
Market participants continue to await a private estimate of the 1997/98 Florida crop by Citrus Consulting International on August 14 for direction.
Fundamentally, traders and analysts said expectations of record 1997/98 crops in Florida and Brazil, combined with a large inventory of juice currently on hand, will continue to dampen sentiment.
On the charts, September support was pegged at 73.50 cents, followed by 71.30 cents, while resistance was seen at 78.00 cents and then 80.00 cents.
An estimated 1,600 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Tuesday's official tally of 2,027 lots.
